title: The Religious System of the Amazulu
shortTitle: The Religious System of the Amazulu
author: Henry Callaway (collector); narrators named in the text

translation.name: The Religious System of the Amazulu — Henry Callaway

rights: Public domain (published 1868–70; collector d. 1890). Scan and OCR: Internet Archive / University of Toronto.
citation: Callaway, Henry. The Religious System of the Amazulu. Springvale, Natal: John A. Blair; London: Trübner, 1868–70. Reprinted for the Folk-Lore Society, 1884.
editorialMarkers: A missionary’s collection of accounts dictated by named Zulu narrators, printed with Callaway’s English facing the Zulu. The Zulu is the primary text; the English is Callaway’s translation and carries his footnotes. Narrators’ names follow their accounts as printed.
method: Layout-aware OCR (DjVu XML word coordinates): running heads set the parts; lines split into left column, right column and full width by position; paragraphs by indent and vertical gap; Zulu paragraphs paired with the facing English by vertical position; narrators’ centred names attach to the preceding accounts; numbered full-width lines at the foot are footnotes attached to the verse carrying the number; paragraphs continue across pages when the previous does not end in terminal punctuation. The scan’s own damage is repaired through scripts/ingest/repair.mjs: the translator’s footnotes and the publisher’s catalogue, which are not the author’s text; words split by the gutter; and letters the scanner misread where the printed word is not in doubt — a token no lexicon knows with exactly one candidate. Anything ambiguous is left as scanned, and every repair is counted in this record..
